fixes.explanation: Yes, friend. The disciples say, “Some say John the Baptist; others say Elijah; and still others, one of the prophets.” John the Baptist is the one who preached in the wilderness (Mark 1:4). So that's one of the names people were saying about Jesus.

Close, but Nehemiah never makes the list. He's the man who led the rebuilding of Jerusalem's wall (Nehemiah 2:17). The disciples name John the Baptist, Elijah and one of the prophets. Nehemiah isn't in that list, baker.
That's him! Jesus asks, “Who do you say I am?” and Peter is the one who answers. Peter is one of the twelve (Mark 3:16). Out of all of them, Peter is the one the text shows answering.
Andrew is one of the twelve too (Mark 3:18), so good thinking. But this time the text says Peter answered. Andrew doesn't speak up in these verses. Right group, wrong disciple, friend.
Right! Peter answers Jesus, “You are the Christ.” The disciples had just told Jesus what other people were saying, and Peter gave Him this answer instead. That's a big answer, baker.

That's what some people were saying. The disciples told Jesus that some said “…one of the prophets.” But when Jesus asks them directly, Peter says something different: “You are the Christ.” The people's answer and Peter's answer aren't the same batch.

Yes, friend. After Peter's answer, the text says Jesus “…warned them not to tell anyone about Him.” That's the opposite of telling everyone. The text doesn't give a reason, so I'll leave it right there.

I see why you'd think so, since Peter took Him aside. But Jesus doesn't agree. He turns, looks at His disciples and rebukes Peter: “Get behind Me, Satan! For you do not have in mind the things of God, but the things of men.” That's a no, friend.
It sounds like it should be true. Hold on to your life and you keep it, right? But Jesus says the opposite: “…whoever wants to save his life will lose it…” He flips it right over.
Right. Jesus says, “If anyone is ashamed of Me and My words in this adulterous and sinful generation…” It's a serious line, so I'll keep my jokes in the oven.

That's it. Jesus says, “…there are some standing here who will not taste death before they see the kingdom of God arrive with power.” He opens with “Truly I tell you…” so He's saying it plainly. The time He gives is before some of those standing there taste death, friend.
